2.0.s.en: 1. The measuring of Jerusalem and its glory:

2.0.0.en: 1 I lifted up mine eyes again, and looked, and behold a man with a measuring line in his hand. 2 Then said I, “Whither goest thou?” And he said unto me, “To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof, and what is the length thereof.” 3 And, behold, the angel that talked with me went forth, and another angel went out to meet him, 4 and said unto him, “Run, speak to this young man, saying, Jerusalem shall be inhabited as towns without walls for the multitude of men and cattle therein: 5 for I, saith the LORD, will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her.

2.0.1.en: The Lord Christ Himself comes forward as a man with a measuring line in His hand to build His house in us by His Holy Spirit, that it may correspond to His heavenly house which St. John saw, the heavenly Jerusalem (Rev 11:1-2; 21:15; etc.).

2.0.2.en: The prophet says, “I lifted up mine eyes and looked,” repeating this phrase in more than one place (Zech 1:18; 2:1; 5:1; 6:1). Since this book proclaims the evangelical thought concerning the salvation of the world, it would not have been possible for the prophet Zechariah to grasp it unless God lifted up his inner eyes by the spirit of prophecy to see and understand God’s thought toward man. I say it is a call directed to all of us to lift up our eyes by the Holy Spirit, so that our understanding may not stop at the limits of the letter but enter into the hidden mysteries of God and look upon His saving works, things that cannot be experienced with eyes blinded in the dust of this world.

2.0.3.en: He saw “a man with a measuring line in his hand” [1]. Perhaps this man is the Word of God, who for our sake became man. He is the one whom he had seen before riding upon a red horse, standing among the myrtle trees that were in the bottom (Zech 1:8), who has come to plan the buildings of His holy Church. St. Didymus the Blind says: [He is the Lord the Savior to whom the prophet Zechariah points by his saying: “Behold the man whose name is The Branch; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the LORD” (Zech 6:12, Septuagint). He is the true light of whom John the Baptist speaks: “This was he of whom I spake, He that cometh after me is preferred before me: for he was before me” (Jn 1:15). He is the builder of Jerusalem, who drew the foundation and laid it as an architect. Since Jerusalem was torn down by the enemies who besieged it, He measures its length and breadth in order to lay the foundations upon which the walls are raised in the proper places, with order and arrangement. St. Paul the Apostle writes of this city for which all who pleased the Lord by their faith were waiting: “which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God” (Heb 10:11). The prophet Ezekiel also says: “and, behold, there was a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of brass, with a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed; and he stood in the gate” (Ezek 40:3)].

2.0.4.en: In the book of Revelation we see the holy temple and the altar measured with a rod, while the outer court is cast out and not measured (Rev 11:1-2), as though our Lord Jesus wants to reassure us that the true children of God who have been sanctified to Him are kept and known to Him, while those who are outside the faith are outside the measure, not worthy to be the subject of His knowledge… Therefore He rebukes them saying: “I know you not whence ye are” (Lk 13:27).

2.0.5.en: As for the measuring reed, it is of gold (Rev 21:15), that is, heavenly, because spiritual and heavenly things are measured only by what is spiritual.

2.1.0.en: What is the measuring line or spiritual measuring reed held by our Architect for the raising up of the holy Jerusalem but the holy Cross, which is made of two beams, one lengthwise and one crosswise? By this Cross He defines the dimensions of His holy city in us, saying: “To measure Jerusalem, to see what is the breadth thereof, and what is the length thereof” [2]. On the crosswise beam of the wood of the Cross the Lord Christ stretched out His hands to gather with the one the Jews and with the other the Gentiles, that all together might be one in Him. As St. Irenaeus says: [He who gathers all things in Himself was hanged on the tree]. And Pope Athanasius: [It was fitting for the Lord to stretch out His hands… that with the one He might gather the ancient people and with the other the Gentiles, and unite them together in Himself]. This is the breadth of the new Jerusalem, for it is fitting for the believer to bear the mark of his crucified Savior, stretching out his hands in love to embrace all humanity in his heart as his brethren. As for the lengthwise wood, upon it the body of the Lord was nailed, lifted up above the earth, fulfilling His promise: “And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me” (Jn 12:32), accomplishing reconciliation between the Father and man in His crucified body. As St. Hippolytus says: [The Cross is Jacob’s ladder; this tree with heavenly dimensions rose from the earth to heaven, setting itself up as an eternal planting between heaven and earth, that it might lift up the whole world]. This is the length of the new Jerusalem, where it is fitting for us to be nailed with Him on the wood, to accept the opening of heaven upon earth and the rising of earth to heaven. It is as though the dimensions of our new Jerusalem are, in its breadth, the widening of our heart to every person, and its length is its opening to heaven; in other words, it is the practice of the commandment of love in Christ Jesus our Lord, a love for all humanity in the heavenly God.

2.2.0.en: The prophet Zechariah continues his discourse by saying: “And, behold, the angel that talked with me went forth, and another angel went out to meet him, and said unto him, Run, speak to this young man, saying, Jerusalem shall be inhabited as towns without walls for the multitude of men and cattle therein: for I, saith the LORD, will be unto her a wall of fire round about, and will be the glory in the midst of her” [4-5].

2.2.1.en: What a vision that gladdens the heart, for it reveals the work of God with us!

2.2.2.en: First: His sending of the angels, for one angel goes forth and another behind him, and the subject of their discourse is our Jerusalem, the dwelling of God with men. In the book of Revelation we see the angels in continual movement, declaring their longing for the last day or the harvest (Rev 14:15-20), longing to see the bride crowned with glory together with her Bridegroom.

2.2.3.en: Perhaps the first angel refers to the heavenly ones who waited for the fulfillment of the prophecies to rejoice at the salvation of man and his return to communion with them in their liturgies and praises of God, while the second angel refers to them as they went forth in the New Testament rejoicing at the fulfillment of what they had long awaited.

2.2.4.en: Second: most likely by the young man here [4] is meant the prophet Zechariah or the believer in general. For if the Lord Christ shared in humanity, becoming an embryo, then a child, a boy, a youth, and a man, yet He did not become an old man according to the body, so that His bride may always remain in a spiritually renewed youth, without the old age of helplessness and weakness, and each member of her sings, saying: “Though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day” (2 Cor 4:16), “But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint” (Isa 40:31), “thy youth is renewed like the eagle’s” (Ps 103:5).

2.2.5.en: St. Didymus the Blind says: [The holy man is a young man in the sight of God’s angels, especially when he puts on the new man, and then it can be said of him: “Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right” (Prov 20:11)… And John the Apostle says in his epistle about those who advance in virtue: “I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one” (1 Jn 2:14). So whoever is young in the Spirit receives the teachings of the angel who goes forth to reveal to him the revelations that we see in the rest of the prophecy.”

2.2.6.en: Third: He reveals to us the dimensions of the new Church, saying: “Jerusalem shall be inhabited as towns without walls for the multitude of men and cattle therein.” She becomes like open country not bounded by a material wall because of its being crowded with men and cattle, for she is the city of love without limits. The soul carries within it the Kingdom of God, widened by love for all, with a glorious inner joy. As for her being crowded with men and cattle, it refers to the sanctification of the soul with unlimited energies and the sanctification of the body, which was animal, with new possibilities without limit. It is as though our inner Jerusalem has room for every person, through the sanctification of soul and body together with all their possibilities and gifts.

2.3.0.en: Fourth: if our inner Jerusalem is like open country not bounded by material walls, yet it has a unique wall. “For I, saith the LORD, will be unto her a wall of fire round about” [5]. This is the wall of fire which the Only-Begotten Son sent to us from the Father after His ascension, when it came upon the disciples in the form of tongues of fire on the day of Pentecost, to surround the Church on every side, to keep her from every evil dart, and to kindle her with the continual warmth of the Spirit. Therefore the believer sings: “By my God have I leaped over a wall” (Ps 18:29), “The LORD is the strength of my life” (Ps 27:1), and as St. Jerome says: [The enemies have besieged me; thou art therefore my fortress.] The enemies have aimed their fiery arrows at my heart, but the divine fire surrounds me as a wall to devour the fire of evil and consume it, as the rod of Moses, which became a serpent, devoured the serpents of the magicians! Thus instead of the deadly fire of evil, he is kindled with the holy divine fire.

2.3.1.en: God is a wall of fire around us, kindling our heart with the fire of love, so that we do not become like those of whom it was said: “the love of many shall wax cold” (Mt 24:12).

2.3.2.en: Thus by this divine wall the enemy has no hope against us, saying: “I will go up to the land of unwalled villages; I will go to them that are at rest, that dwell safely, all of them dwelling without walls, and having neither bars nor gates, to take a spoil, and to take a prey…” (Ezek 38:11-12).

2.3.3.en: Fifth: the Lord says, “and will be the glory in the midst of her” [5]. If the Lord Christ is the pearl of great price which we possess within us, then by His divine fires surrounding us no one is able to gaze upon this pearl shining within us because of its surpassing beauty and its radiance that cannot be looked upon. His splendor becomes our splendor, and His glory is on our account, saying to us as to His bride: “and thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom. And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord GOD” (Ezek 16:13-14).

2.4.0.en: 6 Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the LORD: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the LORD. 7 Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon. 8 For thus saith the LORD of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye. 9 For, behold, I will shake mine hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to their servants: and ye shall know that the LORD of hosts hath sent me.

2.4.1.en: If God Himself has measured the city and surrounded it by His Holy Spirit as a wall of fire and has been revealed in its midst with His glory, all this urges it the more to strive, fleeing from every stumbling block, lest it lose the work of God in it. Therefore He calls to it: “Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north” [6].

2.4.2.en: From the literal historical side, it is a divine call to those who clung to the land of captivity because of their private interests; therefore He calls them to flee from Babylon, “the land of the north,” to the Promised Land; and here He mentions no name or title for them, because by their clinging to a humiliating life they became unworthy of the knowledge of God, and are called “Ho, ho,” like those who are unknown! But from the spiritual side the call is standing and continuing through the ages for every person. As for His repeating the particle of address “Ho,” it is because the call is directed to the Jews as to the Gentiles, that they leave the land of satanic captivity where the cold north wind blows (Sir 43:20), quenching the flame of love in the heart, and go not to another land but to heaven itself, through the fires of the Holy Spirit who lifts it from the land of the north and goes with it from glory to glory to bring it into the bosom of the Father in Christ Jesus our Lord! It is a repeated call that includes the rich as well as the poor, the man as well as the woman, to leave the land of evil with its dust and its mire and return by the Holy Spirit to the divine sanctuaries. This call, as St. Didymus the Blind says, means: [“Flee from evil,” “Depart from evil, and do good” (Ps 34:14), and also: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil” (Isa 1:16)]. This is accomplished by our abstaining from every kind of evil and holding fast to what is praiseworthy, as the Apostle Paul commands: “Prove all things; hold fast that which is good. Abstain from all appearance of evil” (1 Thess 5:21-22). For whoever looks to the good, desiring it and fulfilling it, flees from evil.

2.4.3.en: If God permitted their being scattered as the four winds of heaven because of their evil, He calls them to leave their places and go forth to Zion to enjoy deliverance (salvation), saying: “for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the LORD. Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon” [6-7]. We note in His discourse here the following:

2.4.4.en: First: God wants us to go forth from Babylon, which means confusion and disturbance, to enter Zion, where there is inner peace and a life of joy and praise. St. Didymus says: [The place of salvation is holy Zion, in which those who formerly dwelt with the daughter of Babylon can be saved… And as the name “Babylon” means confusion, everyone whose spirit is troubled is a Babylonian; therefore we must be delivered from this state if we desire to return to Zion; then we shall sing praises and strike the harps in honor of God, for there it is fitting for us to chant to God and play for Him, as it is written: “Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Zion: and unto thee shall the vow be performed” (Ps 65:1), and also: “Sing praises to the LORD, which dwelleth in Zion: declare among the people his doings” (Ps 9:11). It is impossible for us to praise God and play for Him while we dwell with the daughter of Babylon in the north; therefore the Holy Spirit cries with a full voice: Ho, ho, flee from the land of the north, saith the LORD, that you may take refuge in Zion, O dwellers with the daughter of Babylon, for I gather you from the four winds, that is, from the ends of all the earth].

2.4.5.en: Therefore let us flee from the confusion of sin and take refuge in the peace of Zion, where there is the divine fortress, so that the soul may be lifted up to be found in the righteousness of God, enjoying the peace of truth. As St. Jerome says: [As long as we are in the state of grace our soul is at peace, but when we begin to play with sin our soul becomes troubled like a boat battered by the waves].

2.4.6.en: Second: what are the four winds that God permitted to scatter them from Jerusalem but the evil spirits whom God permits to be left to chasten the one who delivers himself to them by his own will? We need not wonder at this, for the Apostle Paul judged the young man who sinned with his father’s wife “to deliver such an one unto Satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus” (1 Cor 5:5). For although the love of God protects us from the power of the wicked one, His providence sometimes permits our being delivered to the bitterness of this enemy to whom we ourselves delivered ourselves, accepting him as our father instead of God our Father (Jn 8:44); then we realize in bitterness our need of the true fatherhood of God.

2.4.7.en: Perhaps by the winds are meant here the strange teachings that shake the soul to break it, which could not affect St. John the Baptist, for the Lord Christ says of him: “What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?” (Mt 11:7). As St. Hilary, bishop of Poitiers, comments: [Did you go out to see a man empty of the knowledge of God, who responds to the breezes of every unclean spirit?] And as St. Augustine comments: [Surely John was not a reed shaken by the wind, for he was not carried about by every wind of doctrine]. And as St. Didymus the Blind says: [The (four winds) may be the different currents of teachings, which make those who walk improperly in thought have evil thoughts and vain works, swaying here and there. The Apostle Paul says: “That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive” (Eph 4:14)].

2.4.8.en: Perhaps by the four winds are meant the trials and afflictions that sweep away and shatter souls built upon the sand and not upon the rock.

2.4.9.en: Perhaps also the four winds refer to the love of the world and the lusts of the body that shake the soul, for we saw that the number (4) refers to these things in our interpretation of the four horns.

2.4.10.en: Third: it is not enough to flee from Babylon; we must flee to Zion, meaning that it is not enough to flee from the confusion of evil, but it is fitting for us to take refuge (Zion) in the righteousness of Christ our Lord. In the positive side of the work St. Paul says: “But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect, and to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel” (Heb 12:22-24). Thus our Lord Jesus by His blood takes us out of evil to bring us into Zion, that we may live on a heavenly level.

2.5.0.en: Finally, since the Lord brings us back from our satanic captivity and brings us into His divine Kingdom, He returns to punish the devil who humbled us, saying: “After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye. For, behold, I will shake mine hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to their servants: and ye shall know that the LORD of hosts hath sent me” [8-9].

2.5.1.en: In our study of some of the books of the prophets we noticed that God, who uses the nations for chastening, when the nations become puffed up against His people returns and punishes these nations.

2.5.2.en: Here He says “after the glory”; perhaps He meant after the Cross, where man was brought back from captivity and God was glorified in him, and at the same time He repaid the devil for his evil by shattering his authority. The enemy who humbled the children of God and spoiled them has become, in Christ Jesus, under humiliation, with no authority over them (Col 2:14-15).

2.5.3.en: What does “toucheth the apple of his eye” mean? The devil, who stretched out his hand to us and made us lose our spiritual sight, has his work rebound upon him, so that his blindness increases day by day, as though by his increasing evil he touches the apple of his own eye until the cup of his blindness is full! And what we say of the devil we say of man: by doing evil to his brother he touches the apple of his own eye and loses spiritual sight, as though, while he is harming his brother’s body or possessions or reputation, he is aiming his blows at his own inner eyes.

2.5.4.en: Evil does not rebound only into the loss of inner sight but also touches his whole being, by the Lord’s saying: “they shall be a spoil to their servants,” for while he thinks that he is shattering his brethren, his servants plunder him. Who are these servants but the senses and emotions of the body, which become uncontrolled because of his evil, so that they rob him of every blessing in him? This is what we observe in practice: when we rage against our brethren, the lusts of the body rage within us and we lose all chastity and self-control, because by our raging against our brethren we lose our mastery over our depths, and the grace of God, the giver of chastity and purity, withdraws!

2.6.0.en: 10 Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion: for, lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith the LORD. 11 And many nations shall be joined to the LORD in that day, and shall be my people: and I will dwell in the midst of thee, and thou shalt know that the LORD of hosts hath sent me unto thee. 12 And the LORD shall inherit Judah his portion in the holy land, and shall choose Jerusalem again. 13 Be silent, O all flesh, before the LORD: for he is raised up out of his holy habitation.

2.6.1.en: If this vision fills the soul with joy, in which the Lord Christ appears as a man with a measuring line in His hand to measure in us His new heavenly Jerusalem, then the secret of true joy is His dwelling in her, for He says: “Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion: for, lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith the LORD” [10]. Fr. John of Kronstadt says: [The mark of sin is disturbance and gloom, while the mark of the righteousness of Christ is inner peace and joy. Thus the Jews hung their harps upon the willows in the land of captivity, for gloom filled their lives, saying: “How shall we sing the LORD’s song in a strange land?” (Ps 136). And by their return to Zion joy returned to them and their lives were turned into praise. St. Didymus the Blind says: [As in the time of the captivity there was lamentation and groaning among the Hebrews because the Lord had departed from the offenders, so at their return to the spiritual mother called Zion He gives them a command to sing and rejoice (sing and rejoice), because the Lord has come and dwelt in her midst, for the temple has indeed been raised up and God has made it His dwelling… The saved captives enjoy this security, saying: “When the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream. Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing” (Ps 126:1-2)… They were groaning when they were scattered from their homeland in the bonds of captivity, so it is natural that they exult and rejoice when they return, for the Lord, the fountain of joy and exultation, has dwelt in their midst]. St. Augustine sees that the praise here is not with the tongue only but with the whole life of man.

2.7.0.en: And the joy does not stop at the man returning from captivity, but extends to his brethren whom he draws with him into the Kingdom of joy, for the prophet says: “And many nations shall be joined to the LORD in that day, and shall be my people: and I will dwell in the midst of thee” [11]. Here he speaks of the return of the Gentiles to the faith and their enjoying, together with their believing brethren of the Jews, God’s dwelling in the midst. And lest the Jews think that by this He has closed the door of faith in their face, He assured them: “And the LORD shall inherit Judah his portion in the holy land, and shall choose Jerusalem again.” If they become the new Judah by their being related to Him who came forth from the tribe of Judah, and if they become the new Jerusalem, they become the inheritance of the Lord and the place of His divine choice.

2.7.1.en: This work seems impossible in the eyes of all: how can the door be opened to all the nations, and they enjoy the dwelling of the Lord in their midst? Therefore He says: “Be silent, O all flesh, before the LORD: for he is raised up out of his holy habitation” [14]. Let every human tongue be silent in fear and trembling, for God, who has declared His care for all humanity through the generations, is working a wonder by opening the door of faith to the Gentiles, so that He appears as one who has awakened to raise humanity from its sleep!
